items.headline: Wuppertal museum restitutes Slevogt painting to heirs of Eduard Fuchs
items.summary: The Von der Heydt-Museum in Wuppertal has returned Max Slevogt's Paradiesvögel (Birds of Paradise, 1900) to the heirs of the Jewish publisher and collector Eduard Fuchs, following an investigation begun in 2020 and a Wuppertal city council decision of 13 July 2026. The painting had been sold under pressure in Berlin in June 1937, when Fuchs needed to raise money for a punitive emigration tax, and was bought there by the dealer Hildebrand Gurlitt; the museum acquired it in 2006. The heirs have consigned the work to Ketterer Kunst's 5 December sale in Munich, with an estimate of €40,000–€60,000.

items.headline: Paris court annuls Sotheby's sale of a Pissarro and orders restitution to the Flavian heirs
items.summary: On 5 November 2026 the Paris Judicial Court annulled Sotheby's London's June 2024 sale (£1.2m) of Camille Pissarro's Darse de pêche et bassin Duquesne, Dieppe (1902) and ordered the painting restituted to the descendants of the Jewish banker Salomon Flavian, whose collection was seized in Paris in 1941. The court found no direct and convincing evidence for the claimed pre-war sales through the Rosenberg gallery and Le Bas, and ordered Sotheby's to disclose the buyer's identity within two months. The claims organisation Mondex has said it intends to appeal.

items.headline: Klimt portrait restituted after the war sets a modern art auction record
items.summary: Gustav Klimt's Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer (1914–16) sold at Sotheby's New York for $236.4 million, a record for a work of modern art at auction, as part of the Leonard A. Lauder Collection sale. The painting had been seized by the Nazis in Vienna and was restituted to Erich Lederer in 1948; this was its first appearance at auction.

items.headline: Museum of Fine Arts, Boston returns two Benin works to the Oba of Benin
items.summary: The Museum of Fine Arts, Boston has returned a bronze relief plaque and a terracotta-and-iron commemorative head to the Oba of Benin, in a ceremony at Nigeria House, New York. Both works are traceable to the 1897 British attack on Benin City and passed through the Pitt-Rivers collection. In April 2025 the museum had also closed its Benin Kingdom Gallery and returned most of a promised gift of Benin works to the donor, because it did not own those works outright.

items.headline: The Netherlands returns 119 Benin Bronzes to Nigeria
items.summary: The Netherlands has returned 119 Benin Bronzes to Nigeria — 113 from the Dutch State Collection and six from the Municipality of Rotterdam — following the recommendation of the independent Colonial Collections Committee; transfer agreements were signed in February 2025. The objects were looted during the 1897 British attack on Benin City. Nigeria's National Commission for Museums and Monuments described it as the largest physical return of Benin artefacts to date; four items remain at the Wereldmuseum on loan.

items.headline: Tate to return a Henry Gibbs painting to the heirs of Samuel Hartveld
items.summary: The UK Spoliation Advisory Panel has recommended, and Tate has supported, returning Henry Gibbs's Aeneas and his family fleeing Burning Troy (1654) to the heirs of the Jewish Belgian collector Samuel Hartveld. Hartveld left the painting behind when he fled Antwerp in 1940; Tate bought it in 1994 from a Brussels gallery. The claim was brought in May 2024 by the Sonia Klein Trust on the family's behalf.
